Olevsk Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zhytomyrska oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Jews are first mentioned in Olevsk in the 18th century, growing from 157 people in 1765 to 1,187 (57 percent) by 1897, supported by a synagogue and Jewish loan fund; the community survived several pogroms during the 1918–21 Civil War and founded two agricultural collectives in Kherson District. By 1939, the Jewish population had grown to 2,858 (42 percent). Following the 1941 German invasion, the town was initially controlled by German-aligned Ukrainian nationalists under Taras Bulba-Borovets in the self-styled 'Olevsk Republic'; Jews who remained were subjected to robbery and violence before being confined to a ghetto once German civil administration arrived that November, where most were murdered. After liberation, Jews returned to Olevsk, reaching about 1,300 (13 percent) by 1959, before most emigrated to the US or Israel by the century's end.
